item.title: Why Must Evil Grow Before It Ends? | Daat Tevunot §161-166
item.description:
Reward and punishment balance good and evil but cannot uproot evil: for that it must be allowed to spread, short of destroying the world, and then be overturned. In that darkness the righteous may suffer regardless of merit, are compensated, and share in rectifying the whole world.

item.title: Why Do Some Righteous Suffer and Others Thrive? | Daat Tevunot §167-168
item.description:
The world is rectified both by increasing the light, when the righteous are rewarded, and by reducing it, when they suffer. Which good person serves through which is decreed by God, and this is mazal; yet since reward and punishment also operate, a sufferer should still pray and repent.

item.title: What Is Mazal, If Not the Stars? | Daat Tevunot §169-170
item.description:
Mazal here is not astrology but the decree of how each person serves the tikkun. God runs the world by two modes, reward and punishment and mazal, so no one can know why he suffers; he must examine his deeds and accept God's judgment wholeheartedly, the real meaning of siduk hadin.

item.title: Does God Forget Anything? | Daat Tevunot §170-171
item.description:
Is a good deed rewarded for all it sets in motion? Reward and punishment weigh every knock-on effect of a deed, both the damage and the repair, and teshuvah alone is the power that makes things forgotten. Then the Neshamah thanks the Sekhel for the principles of the whole book and for settled faith.

item.title: What Is Prophecy? | Daat Tevunot §175-180
item.description:
Prophecy is connection to God and a grasp of His glory, with information only a by-product. The prophet grasps God's traits, not His essence, through images and riddles known without doubt; images of traits and of actions, why trait images come with their meaning, and Moshe without riddles.
